newsitem.title: DENMARK: Foreign buyers lift Danish shares to record levels.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buyers lift Danish shares to record levels.

text.p: Foreign buyers pushed Danish share prices to an all-time closing high on Tuesday, and dealers said Wednesday's trade depended on the direction of the New York market and continued enthusiasm for Danish bank paper.
"Developments in the U.S. will influence tomorrow's trade but if interest in the banks continues at today's level we shall close higher irrespective of what the U.S. does," a dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index gained 1.20 point to 121.74 in overall bourse turnover of 1.039 billion crowns. The KFX September future rose 0.90 point to 121.45 with 365 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
The previous KFX high of 120.59 was set on August 20, after a run of almost daily records.

Den Danske Bank rose 11 crowns to 427 crowns and Unidanmark gained five crowns to 267. Dealers say that many investors feel that their portfolios are light on bank shares and there are relatively few on offer.
"It was mainly foreigners buying them up, they apparently still feel that Danish bank shares are relatively cheap," a dealer said.
Carlsberg rose seven crowns to 357 crowns, matching its July 2 year-high.
Analysts are advising investors to buy at up to 400 crowns.
